content.value_statement: Annotated data workflows can be hard to structure, store, and scale. This skill gives practical AnnData guidance for Python, h5ad, Zarr, and single-cell analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains AnnData object structure, including X, obs, var, layers, obsm, varm, obsp, uns, and raw.
Guides reading and writing h5ad, Zarr, CSV, MTX, Loom, 10X, Excel, and text formats.
Shows memory-aware practices such as sparse matrices, categoricals, backed mode, and lazy reads.
Describes concatenation strategies for batches, variables, labels, joins, and merge behavior.
Provides workflow patterns for single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing, batch integration, and large datasets.
Connects AnnData usage with Scanpy, Muon, PyTorch loaders, and the broader scverse ecosystem.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not validate biological conclusions.
It does not include project-specific schemas, quality thresholds, or laboratory protocols.
Remote data examples require user-provided trusted sources and normal network safety checks.
Some APIs may change across AnnData, Scanpy, or scverse versions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Single-Cell Data
use_cases.description: Plan how to load, annotate, filter, normalize, and save single-cell expression data with AnnData and Scanpy.

use_cases.title: Scale Large Dataset Access
use_cases.description: Choose backed mode, Zarr storage, chunking, and sparse data patterns for datasets larger than memory.

use_cases.title: Standardize Training Examples
use_cases.description: Create clear AnnData examples for object structure, metadata alignment, concatenation, and common pitfalls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic AnnData Object
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for annotated matrix data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AnnData skill to explain how I should create an AnnData object from an expression matrix, cell metadata, and gene metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Read and Save Data Efficiently
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AnnData skill to recommend the best read and write approach for h5ad, Zarr, and CSV data in my Python workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Experimental Batches
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AnnData skill to design a concatenation plan for multiple batches with labels, join settings, and metadata merge rules.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Large Single-Cell Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design for large data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AnnData skill to review my large single-cell analysis plan for memory use, backed mode, sparse storage, raw data handling, and reproducibility.

output_examples.input: I need to store raw counts before filtering highly variable genes.
output_examples.output: The response recommends preserving raw data before filtering, then documenting which variable filter was applied and where processed data is saved.

output_examples.input: I have three batches and need one AnnData object for downstream Scanpy analysis.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a batch concatenation plan with source labels, compatible join choices, and checks for metadata consistency.

output_examples.input: My h5ad file is too large to load into memory.
output_examples.output: The response suggests backed reading, selective metadata filtering, sparse matrices, categorical columns, and loading only the required subset.

best_practices: Use backed mode or Zarr for large datasets, and load only the subset needed for analysis.
Keep observation and variable indices stable when adding external metadata.
Store raw data before filtering or normalization when downstream comparisons require original values.
anti_patterns: Do not assume AnnData views are independent when modifying subsets.
Do not load very large h5ad files fully into memory without checking size and access needs.
Do not merge batches without preserving source labels and verifying metadata alignment.

faq.question: Does this skill run AnnData code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for an assistant to use when helping with AnnData workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with h5ad and Zarr files?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers reading, writing, compression, backed mode, cloud-oriented Zarr storage, and format conversion.

faq.question: Does it replace Scanpy documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes practical AnnData patterns and points users toward the scverse ecosystem for complete API details.

faq.question: Can it help with very large datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes backed mode, lazy reads, sparse matrices, categoricals, and chunking strategies.

faq.question: Does it download remote data by itself?
faq.answer: No. Remote access examples require a user-selected trusted source and normal permission checks.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
